$comment: Reviewed, time-boxed exceptions for `npm run audit:ci`.
Every entry needs a reason, the mitigation that makes it acceptable, and a reviewBy date.
The gate fails when an entry expires, when an allowlisted advisory stops appearing
(the exception is stale and must be deleted), or when its severity changes.
See the 'Dependency audit state' section of README.md for the full analysis.

advisories.title: image-size: ICNS parser allows denial of service through an infinite loop
advisories.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-19. Reached only via metro (the bundler) at build time; not present in the shipped app binary. A patched image-size now exists (2.0.3+, the advisory covers <=2.0.2), but it is a major version: metro 0.84.x, which react-native 0.86.2 pins at ^0.84.3, depends on image-size ^1.0.2, and the 1.x line (1.2.1, the 'legacy' tag) has no fix. Metro 0.87.1 drops image-size entirely, so an RN upgrade onto it removes this advisory. An overrides pin to 2.0.4 was tested against Metro's call shape (CommonJS default export, Buffer in, {width, height} out) and works, but it forces Metro outside its declared range, so it is recorded as an option rather than taken.
advisories.mitigation: metro.config.js calls image-size's disableTypes() on Metro's own instance to switch off the icns parser. Metro never requests dimensions for ICNS assets, so this costs nothing and the payload is rejected instantly instead of looping. The app also currently bundles no image assets outside the native projects, so Metro never calls image-size at all today.

advisories.title: image-size: JXL and HEIF parsers allow denial of service through infinite loops
advisories.reason: Re-reviewed 2026-10-19. Same root cause, package, reachability and fix situation as GHSA-w3rx-r6r6-pgpr.
advisories.mitigation: metro.config.js disables the jxl, jxl-stream and heif parsers alongside icns.

advisories.title: @grpc/grpc-js: In certain configurations, getAuthContext can return unauthorized certificates as though they were authorized
advisories.reason: Transitive via @react-native-firebase/app -> firebase (the Firebase JS SDK) -> @firebase/firestore -> @grpc/grpc-js@1.9.16. The fix is 1.13.6, but @firebase/firestore pins ~1.9.0, so no in-range upgrade exists; npm's fixAvailable is a major downgrade of @react-native-firebase to 20.1.0. Forcing 1.13.6 through overrides would put a library outside its declared range for no runtime benefit (see the mitigation).
advisories.mitigation: Unreachable in the shipped app, three times over. (1) On iOS and Android, RNFB uses the native Firebase SDKs; the JS SDK is only its fallback for other platforms (web, macOS). (2) The app installs only @react-native-firebase/app and /crashlytics; nothing in src/ or in RNFB imports Firestore (only RNFB's own web shim references it, and only the uninstalled @react-native-firebase/firestore package would load that). (3) Even if Firestore were bundled, Metro resolves its 'react-native' entry (dist/index.rn.js), which has no reference to grpc-js; grpc-js is used only by Firestore's Node.js build, and it needs Node's http2 module, which does not exist in a React Native app.

advisories.title: @grpc/grpc-js: The server transmits some error messages thrown by method handlers to the client in status messages
advisories.reason: Same dependency path and fix situation as GHSA-m9gg-hp2v-232j. This one concerns grpc-js acting as a server, which the app never does.
advisories.mitigation: Same as GHSA-m9gg-hp2v-232j: grpc-js is never loaded on iOS or Android.

advisories.title: braces vulnerable to stack-exhaustion denial of service through deeply nested patterns
advisories.reason: Build and test tooling only, never in the shipped app: react-native -> metro -> metro-file-map -> micromatch -> braces, and jest -> micromatch -> braces. The advisory covers <=3.0.3, which is every published version (3.0.3 is the latest), so there is no version to upgrade to. npm's fixAvailable is a downgrade to react-native 0.72.17, which the README's 'Do not run npm audit fix --force' section rules out.
advisories.mitigation: The vulnerable expansion runs only on glob patterns written by this project (Metro's watcher and resolver config, Jest's testMatch and moduleNameMapper), on a developer machine or CI runner. No user-, network- or device-supplied pattern ever reaches it, so there is no attacker to supply a deeply nested one.

advisories.title: sprintf-js vulnerable to denial of service through unbounded precision specifiers
advisories.reason: Test tooling only: @react-native/jest-preset -> babel-jest -> babel-plugin-istanbul -> @istanbuljs/load-nyc-config -> js-yaml@3 -> argparse@1 -> sprintf-js@1.0.3. The advisory covers <=1.1.3, which is every published version, so there is no version to upgrade to; argparse 1.x also pins ~1.0.2.
advisories.mitigation: Never in the shipped app. The path is code-coverage tooling, which this project does not enable (the test script is plain `jest`, with no collectCoverage), and even then sprintf-js only formats argparse's own help text from fixed format strings, never input from outside the repo.
